title: Runs too slow or too costly: what kind of fix fits?
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Simple requests run the full pipeline
Coordinator selects subagents by query complexity
Cost matters and nobody waits for results
Someone is waiting for the answer
Time becomes the slowest, not the sum
rule: When requests vary in complexity, let the coordinator choose which subagents each one needs. Use batch only when nobody is waiting.

title: Understanding unfamiliar code: which strategy fits the goal?
head: Goal
Right strategy
Why
rows: Answer one specific question or bug
Grep for entry points, then Read along the flow
Context goes only to relevant code
Get a broad map of a large area
Verbose discovery stays out of the main context
/compact or a scratchpad of key findings
Narrow the scope; restart from findings
Need to design a change across many files
Plan mode (with Explore if discovery is heavy)
rule: For a specific question, Grep for the entry point and Read along the flow. Reading everything first wastes the context you need.

title: Splitting a multi-step job: fixed chain or adaptive plan?
head: Situation
Right structure
Why
rows: Same steps, same order for every item
Next step depends on what is found
A step must always run first
rule: Fixed steps in a fixed order: chain them, one job per call. Save adaptive coordinators for work whose steps depend on what is found.

title: Fixed steps or adaptive steps?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Regular, predictable work, e.g. same check per file
Large code change, several valid designs
Many files to review at once
Per-file passes plus an integration pass
rule: If findings change what to do next, generate the steps from the findings.

title: One growing prompt: is it a layout problem or a fit problem?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Long prompt, key items missed mid-way
Classify, then route to a focused prompt
rule: When one prompt serves several kinds of input and its parts conflict, classify first and route each input to a focused prompt.

title: Big analysis came back uneven: how should the work be split?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Fixed list of items, uneven depth, contradictions
Scope unknown; next steps depend on findings
Discovery output floods the main chat
Findings lost across long sessions or restarts
Same session reviews its own work
rule: For a fixed list of items, give each its own pass, then run one pass that compares them.

title: Can the steps be listed before the work starts?
head: Situation
Decomposition
Why
rows: Same structure every time, all inputs present
Inputs present but out of order
Fixed chain with sorting + integration pass
Reading reveals new work (missing documents to fetch)
rule: Use fixed chains when the steps are known up front; use adaptive decomposition when reading reveals new work.

title: How should the coordinator split the work?
head: Situation
Decomposition
Why
rows: Same steps every time; must be auditable
Next step depends on what was just found
Refinement loop: find gaps, re-delegate, re-synthesize
Fills what the first pass missed
Requests vary from one fact to a full review
Skip what a request doesn't need
rule: Known, independent steps: fixed pipeline. Steps that depend on findings: adaptive plan.
